p: Benjamin: He speaks to them chiefly because they should take heed by the example of their brethren the other half of their tribe, who were now carried away prisoners.
Tekoa: Which was a city in Judah, six miles from Bethlehem, 2Ch 11:6.
Bethhaccerem: Read Ne 3:14.
a comely and delicate woman: I have intreated her gently, and given her abundance of all things.
shall come to her: She will be so destroyed that the sheep may be fed in her.
Prepare ye war against her: He speaks this in the person of the Babylonians, who complain that the time fails them before they have brought their enterprises to pass.
violence and destruction is heard in: He shows the reason why it would be destroyed, and how it comes from themselves.
Jerusalem: He warns them to amend by his correction, and turn to him by repentance.
back thy hand as a grapegatherer: He exhorts the Babylonians to be diligent to search out all and to leave none.
uncircumcised: They delight to hear vain things, and to shut up their ears to true doctrine.
I will pour it out upon: As the Lord had given him his word to be as a fire of his indignation to burn the wicked, Jer 5:14 so he kindles it now when he sees that all remedies are past.
children abroad: No one will be spared.
Peace: When the people began to fear God's judgments, the false prophets comforted them by flatterings, showing that God would send peace and not war.
old paths: In which the patriarchs and prophets walked, directed by the word of God: signifying that there is no true way, but that which God prescribes.
watchmen over you: Prophets who would warn you of the dangers that were at hand.
nations: God takes all the world to witness and the insensible creatures of the ingratitude of the Jews.
incense from Sheba: Read Isa 1:11, Am 5:21.
north country: From Babylon by Dan, which was north of Jerusalem.
feeble: For fear of the enemy: he speaks this in the person of the Jews.
thee for a tower and a: Meaning, Jeremiah, whom God had appointed to try out the godly from the wicked, as a founder does the pure metal from the dross.
bellows is burned: All the pain and labour that has been taken with them is lost.
